summary: Manik Man Bajracharya works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. Affiliated with the Lotus Research Centre, he held posts attested at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2018 and Heidelberg University in 2023.

Manlio Iofrida is a philosopher who studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore (~1970–1975). He held academic posts at the University of Pisa (~1979–1987) and the University of Bologna (~1988).

Manshi Kiyozawa (1863–1903) was a Japanese scholar of Buddhism and philosophy. He studied at Otani University, Toyo University, and the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He later served as Otani University's founding president (1901–1902).
Manu Leumann (1889–1977) was a linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).

Marc Aurel Stein (1862–1943) was an archaeologist, Indologist, and Iranian specialist. After earning his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, he headed Oriental College (1888–1899) and served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1904, 1910–1912).
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2016 under the doctoral supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and was also taught by Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen (1884–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954) and the University of Paris (~1926–1954).

Marcel Granet (1884–1940) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.
Marcel Hofinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte.

Marcel Mauss (1872–1950) was a French scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under Émile Durkheim and Sylvain Lévi. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1901–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1940).

Marcelle Lalou (1890–1967) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. She later taught at the EPHE from 1938 to 1963.
Marco Ferrante is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who held posts at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2014) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Marco Walther is a Tibetologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcus Bingenheimer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Würzburg, Nagoya University, and Heidelberg University, and held posts at the Chung-Hwa Institute, Dharma Drum Institute, and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marek Mejor is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He held a junior research fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982), and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil (1952–2011) was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Sheffield and subsequently served on its faculty from around 1986 until 2011.
Margaret Cone is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts attested in 1996 at the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge.
Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.
